mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants anticipate cheaper corporate financing and expanded investment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that typically precede corporate earnings contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as risk appetite diminishes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through stronger earnings visibility.
failure_condition: The joint growth of HOUST and RSAFS above 50th percentiles fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) during supply chain disruptions causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as manufacturing output contraction pressures corporate margins and growth expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0%) indicates sustained economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved business confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% triggers immediate market expectations of aggressive rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as discount rates rise and risk assets face pressure.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS > 0.3%) and declining unemployment (UNRATE < 0.2pp change) signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint movement of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to yield positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0%) combine to increase real borrowing costs and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. baseline).
